title: Urteilsradar: the lawyer’s workspace
notes:
SLIDE 1 · 120 seconds · 00:00–02:00 · Paul
00:00–00:25 [Show the list.] This is our result: Urteilsradar, a workspace for the lawyer. On the left are the rulings, sorted by relevance. The most useful ruling opens immediately, so the lawyer can start reading without configuring the screen.
00:25–00:55 [Point to the details and switch language.] On the right is the selected ruling, with its relevance reason, metadata and summary. German and French summaries are available in the same detail view. Links to the considerations connect the summary with the underlying ruling.
00:55–01:20 [Point to Bearbeiten and Verlauf.] The lawyer can edit the summary and inspect its history. That makes the generated text a draft they can take responsibility for, with the corrections recorded.
01:20–01:45 [Show borderline cases and Nicht relevant without saving.] We distinguish ordinary relevant cases from borderline cases. The second category preserves uncertain cases for a lawyer's attention. Nicht relevant removes an unwanted case from the working list. The current confirmation action is labelled Erledigt.
01:45–02:00 [Point to add-ruling and Trefferliste.] Additional rulings can be summarised, and the hit list exports as CSV. Next we will explain the algorithms behind the selection and order.

title: Four passes collect and review evidence
notes:
SLIDE 2 · 40 seconds · 02:00–02:40 · Miguel
The selection uses four Apertus passes. Triage assesses overall relevance. A separate invalidity pass checks IV rulings for rules that transfer to accident insurance. ATSG rescue then revisits candidates those earlier passes rejected, requiring a quotation from the ruling. Critical review compares this evidence with the actual considerations and operative part. The final selection preserves the earlier positives, adds plausible cases as borderline cases and excludes the rest. The three evidence boxes are separate views, not three unconditional parallel jobs.

title: A separate ranker orders the selected cases
notes:
SLIDE 3 · 40 seconds · 02:40–03:20 · Miguel
Selection tells us what enters the list. A separate algorithm decides what comes first. Apertus assesses relevance, importance, legal substance, broad impact and procedural value. The selected ranker learns how to weight these assessments, together with facts such as a five-judge panel, from Suva's yes-or-no decisions. We compare the learned model with triage-only and importance-based ranking through repeated cross-validation. Separately, blind rankings from other models check whether the resulting order makes sense. Relevant cases lead the list, and borderline cases remain below them.

title: Other models benchmark the final ranking
notes:
SLIDE 4 · 30 seconds · 03:20–03:50 · Miguel
We asked Codex, Gemini, Muse and Claude to rank the same rulings blind. To combine them, we normalise each model's scores to percentile ranks, then take a weighted average. The weights reflect calibration performance on labelled rulings. The graph compares their June top tens with the final Apertus list. Orange shows Apertus itself as the ten-case reference. We use consensus disagreements to fine-tune the algorithm through prompt and ranking refinements. In that development sense, Apertus learns from the comparison. The runtime still uses Apertus, not the reference models.

title: Our summaries retain the key legal points
notes:
SLIDE 5 · 40 seconds · 03:50–04:30 · Miguel
The message is that our summaries retain most of the legal substance in Suva’s expert summaries. Coverage measures retained key legal points, not overall factual accuracy. First, Apertus extracts two to six key legal points from each Suva expert summary. In a separate judging call, it checks our summary against those points. Each point earns one for covered, half for partial and zero for missing. We average within a ruling, then across the held-out rulings. That gives 94.7 percent mean coverage across 19 examples. The expert comparison below shows the same ruling on both sides. We also check outcomes, consideration references and insurer names automatically.
